prerequisites: Analyzing linear and non-linear electronic circuits

learning_outcomes.text: The students will deepen their knowledge and understanding of the behaviour and usage of digital electronic circuits and systems (memories, microcontrollers, reconfigurable platforms), as well as the basis of their design and programming techniques.

Students must be able to design digital electronic circuits, both by choosing discrete components from available commercial offerings, and using software or hardware programmable components, using languages such as C and VHDL.
The student must also be able to apply the acquired knowledge to understand the workings of the buses most commonly used to interconnect electronic systems and devices.

The solution of real-world design problems, that include the detailed analysis of the digital portions of a "case study" (whose analog part is dealt with in the "Analog Electronic Circuits and Systems" course) stimulates the student's ability to integrate knowledge acquired in this and in preceding courses, so as to reach a complete and rational design solution, based on the available scientific literature and device data sheets.

syllabus_topics: Electrical characteristics of logic gates: Propagation delay times, power consumption, buffers, transmission gates, clock feedthrough.
Arithmetic circuits: adders, subtracters, multipliers, comparators, shifters.
Memories: Organization, decoders, basic memory cell, sense amplifiers.
Memory interfaces: parallel (SRAM, DRAM, NAND) and serial (SPI, I2C) buses.
Programmable devices: FPGA architecture and design methods.
Implementation of peripherals (SPI and I2C transceivers).
Design guidelines: Synchronous circuits, clock buffering, synchronizers, reset.
Case study: Design of the digital part of an ECG signal acquisition system.
Design of buffers and simple digital circuits.
HW/SW cosimulation of an I2C bus and EEPROM memories.

assessment_methods.method: Written paper (VHDL-based design project or exercises)
Oral test (discussion of written paper and course topics)

assessment_rules: The evaluation method comprises two tests: a written paper and an oral test. The written paper can be a VHDL-based design project or written exercises. The oral test includes the discussion of the written paper and other course topics, and must be undertaken during the same exam session as the written test. The final mark will be the mark obtained in the oral test. Honors will be granted to students who achieve the maximum mark in the oral test and demonstrate excellent mastery of the subject.
